Identified as this saint because: A Byzantine bronze pilgrim stamp in the Walters Art Museum, not an icon; Commons' description reads 'St. Isidore was martyred on the Greek island of Chios in AD 251' and the file is in Category:Isidore of Chios — the soldier martyr of 14 May. Commons describes it: St. Isidore was martyred on the Greek island of Chios in AD 251. The well into which his body was thrown later became a healing shrine, represented at the right. The ship to the left refers to Isidore's role as patron saint of sailors, as well as to the ships that carried pilgrims to his island shrine.
